subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 2: WOW! Team Talk – Saving energy
outcomes: Understand a dialogue about a school energy-saving competition.
React with Brilliant!, I know! and Me too!
Suggest ideas to save energy at school.

tf.s: The competition is to see which school can save the most energy.
tf.why: Yes, the schools compete to save energy.

tf.s: The children are going to close doors to keep the classroom warm.
tf.why: They close doors to keep the classroom cool.

tf.s: The children already have recycling boxes for paper.
tf.why: Right! They have paper recycling boxes.

tf.s: Eric wants to throw away the plastic bottles.
tf.why: Eric says they shouldn’t throw them away.

tf.s: Ali tells Eric to turn off the computer.
tf.why: Yes, he hopes Eric isn’t going to forget.

tf.s: The children are going to put their ideas on the WOW! website.
tf.why: Correct! Their ideas go on the WOW! website.

tf.s: We say “Me too!” when we do or feel the same thing.
tf.why: Great! Me too! shows you are the same.

tf.s: “Brilliant!” is a sad reaction to bad news.
tf.why: Brilliant! shows you think something is great.

tf.s: Switching off lights is one of the children’s ideas to save energy.
tf.why: Yes, switching off lights saves energy.

boxes.q: Why are they going to close doors?
boxes.why: Closed doors keep the cool air in.

boxes.q: What recycling boxes do they already have?
boxes.why: They already have paper recycling boxes.

boxes.q: Where will they put their ideas?
boxes.why: They will share ideas on the WOW! website.

boxes.q: Which expression shows you do the same thing?
boxes.why: Me too! means the same is true for me.

boxes.q: Reply: “I came first in the running race.”
boxes.why: Brilliant! shows you are happy for your friend.

boxes.q: A: How can we use less paper? B: ___! We can do our homework online.
boxes.why: I know! is used here to give a good idea.

boxes.q: Reply: “I’m going to the park this afternoon.”
boxes.why: Me too! means you are going as well.

boxes.q: What should they do with the plastic bottles?
boxes.why: Eric says they shouldn’t throw them away.

boxes.q: Which action saves energy in class?

boxes.why: Schools compete to save the most energy.

hunt.q: Say you do the same thing
Close doors to keep the room…

mcq.q: What competition are the children going to take part in?
o: A competition to see which school can save the most energy

mcq.q: Who tells Eric to turn off the computer?
mcq.why: Ali reminds Eric to turn it off.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the children’s ideas?
o: Leave the lights on all day
mcq.why: The children want to save energy, not waste it.

mcq.q: A: “I love reading WOW! Magazine.” B: “___ I read it every week.”
mcq.why: B does the same thing, so Me too! fits.

mcq.q: A: “I recycled all our plastic bottles.” B: “___”
A: “How can we save water?” B: “___ We can have quick showers.”
Why does Ali remind Eric to turn off the computer?
o: He hopes Eric isn’t going to forget, so they can save energy.
He wants Eric to play a game.
He wants to use the computer himself.
mcq.why: Turning off computers is part of their energy-saving plan.

mcq.q: Which new idea best fits the school energy competition?
o: Use the stairs instead of the lift.
Leave the computers on at night.
Leave the lights on after school.

mcq.q: Why does Eric say they shouldn’t throw away the plastic bottles?
o: They can recycle them to help the planet.
mcq.why: Plastic bottles can be recycled instead of thrown away.
